data.narrative:
Theseus is a Seed-stage Defense & Security company founded by Stanford and McGill engineers, having raised $4.3M to date. The valuation analysis benchmarks against a peer universe of 10 private and 2 public comparables in the same sector and adjacent stages, including UFORCE, Singularity, and NODA AI.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for Seed-to-next-stage advancement, using the $4.3M raised as a proxy baseline, yielding $11M. Peer-median analysis draws from three same-sector peers at Seed and Series A stages: UFORCE ($1.0B), Singularity ($400M), and NODA AI ($125M), producing a median valuation of $400M with a range of $125M to $1.0B.

The two methods produce a wide spread, reflecting the substantial uncertainty inherent in early-stage defense-tech valuations where comparable companies span three orders of magnitude. The triangulated range anchors to $9M (low), $205M (median), and $460M (high). The stage-progression method suggests conservative floor valuation near current raised capital, while peer-median pulls materially higher given strong sector dynamics. Key uncertainties include Theseus's differentiation within the crowded defense-AI landscape, product maturity relative to comparables, and the applicability of late-stage peer valuations to an early-stage company. A valuation toward the lower-to-middle quartile of the peer range may be more defensible absent evidence of exceptional product-market fit.
